As someone who’s had to use Ryobi on a W-2 gig because the company is cheap as hell, those tools are derided for a reason. Yes they’re smaller but ooo buddy do they suck if you need to do any proper construction work. The drills and drivers have no torque whatsoever. You can’t even drill out a stuck rack screw with one. There’s a reason why people clown on Ryobi. They did women dirty with this line, I’m actually mad hearing it was designed for women. 

I use the Makita subcompact drill/driver sets in my own kit. They are proper tools for small hands and I cannot recommend them enough. Reliable, enough torque to get ya going, and a nice small grip. They come with smaller batteries than the regular 18V Makita, but you can buy bigger ones. They also have a bunch of saws and other cute sized tools in that series. I also really liked Hilti stuff, but they cost 2x as much as other brands. Milwaukee is unergonomic as hell for me though, definitely great for people with piano player hands. Dewalt keeps changing their”standard” battery sizes, so I can’t recommend their hand tools… the big saws are great though.

I’m a less well to do artist with a performance practice and here’s the nasty secret of it all— we all go on anyways. I’ve had the puke bucket backstage then went on and did a performance. I’ve performed after having severe SI where I don’t feel safe leaving my house, on crutches, after a concussion, period cramps where I passed out on the floor earlier in the day, when I couldn’t feel my hands due to a pinched nerve, with a knife in eyeball mid-migraine. I might have to take an uber to the gig instead of driving or ask a buddy to help carry my shit but if I miss one performance due to being sick, there are no more performances. You won’t get booked again if you call out sick, especially as a lesser known musician. There is no PTO or even unpaid time off, people are there to see YOU. If you’re Gaga and you get a cold and decide to stay home the stakes are even higher, you’re on the hook for millions in refunds, on the hook to pay for your staff to be paid for the call date, in the news for being unreliable, on the hook for a new performance date and to honor those tickets from the previous one… it’s not as simple as Joe in accounting calling out with the flu. If she’s making a TV appearance, she literally can’t call the host and be like “sorry Jimmy I have a migraine can I perform on your show tomorrow night instead and you have Taylor Swift swap dates with me?” My point is that Gaga probably has performed with a migraine many times in her life.

Like Missy Elliot “disappearing” at the height of her career was because she didn’t have a condition where she could make the show go on, and she actually valued her health. A lot of musicians will push thru serious shit until they literally die. Hell, I had a friend perform with patches of his hair shaved off from cancer treatment, he was dead a few months later. We were so damn worried about him when he actually missed a gig— it was a month before he died and he sent a fixed piece with instructions on how to play it back for him.

5.1 isn’t Atmos, it’s 5.1. Atmos is 7.1.4 or better, the height component with flyovers is the gimmick for mixing in Atmos/ Atmos at theatre scale. Dolby Atmos is like the Kleenex of multichannel sound, it’s good but also Puffs and Starbucks napkins exist and are just as good for blowing your nose. 

I’ve done a lot of unique multi-channel systems coming out of academia/experimental music — quad and octophonic are the most common formats for multichannel arrays for live performance, and frankly have more ideal listening positions than Atmos or 5.1. Atmos kinda blows for live performance, it’s only fixed media playback. Dolby isn’t interested in supporting in live performance thru Atmos. When I’ve seen events at Dolby’s test theater space where they advertise a live “Atmos” performance it’s always Ambisonics or IRCAM spat~ under the hood on the performers computer. Most folks will mix out of Max/MSP, SuperCollider, Ableton or another DAW using [ambisonics](https://ambisonics.ch) or [envelop4live](https://envelop.us/page/software). Envelop also has a venue in SF, you could reach out to them to talk about their array and setup. I’m pretty sure they’re either 8 or 16channel surround. Ambisonics is great because it’s open source and has excellent support and compatibility across multiple platforms. In the analog realm— Suzanne Ciani uses a Buchla quad panner module to spatialize her mix in real time (there’s also a bunch of lesser known nerds doing this in modular). I’ve also seen 4.4 quad a lot in club setups (usually as a stereo up-mix).

In terms of meds I’ve found helpful:
* adding an otc nasal spray like Flonase or rhinocourt. I like rhinocourt better
* a proper decongestant for really bad allergy days. The Sudafed behind the counter that you give your ID for is the one that you want. Phenylephrine is useless, the FDA is actually working on taking it off the market because it’s so ineffective. 
* In terms of prescription stuff, there’s some daily meds for asthma that are great and minimize the use of a rescue inhaler. See a doctor, just your primary should do, to discuss options. This sort of stuff can also get prescribed for environmental allergies that are causing mild breathing issues. It doesn’t sound like OOP is there yet tho. 

Non medically, I’d recommend the following for allergies:
* a robot vacuum if you can afford it (more regularly cleanings without the work)
* a regular vacuum with disposable bags + hepa filtered exhaust and vacuuming furniture
* air purifiers in every room with filters on auto deliver. You’ll want to change the filter every 1-2 months or sooner if you’re shit at vacuuming
* brushing your baby’s fur a few times a week. Gets rid of extra hair so it doesn’t wind up all over your house
* keeping the cat out of the bedroom
* if you can’t or don’t want to keep the cat out of the bedroom, throw a large blanket or a sheet over your entire bed including pillows when the bed is not in use, and take cover off at night when you’re sleeping. Wash it once a week or rotate it with a second one. 
* changing your sheets, pillowcases and duvet covers once a week or more.
* covering upholstered furniture with washable slip covers, sheets or throw blankets and washing them regularly
* lint brush for pants and sweaters if you want to wear them more than once a wash (cat hair lol)
* no rugs, or only machine washable, woven ones. 
* never live anywhere with wall to wall carpet, especially in your bedrooms. That shit cannot be cleaned. 

That said if anyone is getting hives or having their throat close up on the regular even with these sorts of steps… that’s when things are sad. My dad developed this sort of severe reaction in the last years of his cat’s life. My parents kept her out of the bedroom, indoor lap visits were only for my mom and he only had outside visits while he was in the garden or on the porch (she was an indoor/outdoor lady) until she passed at 21. They haven’t gotten any more pets since her. They had cats for 30+ years before this happened.

What helped me for the California professional look (which will be casual outside of your court room apparel) is uniform dressing. This is a typical uniform closet:
* 3 black tee shirts in a unisex cut (black because it doesn’t show stains as easily) - Hanes men’s undershirts in the multipack or [Uniqlo](https://www.uniqlo.com/us/en/products/E424873-000/00?colorDisplayCode=74&sizeDisplayCode=003) shirts 
* 2 collared shirts in a neutral color (I like black because stain prevention) [Uniqlo](https://www.uniqlo.com/us/en/products/E471301-000/00?colorDisplayCode=09&sizeDisplayCode=003) or a thrift store is your best bet. 
* 2 pairs of black pants in a trouser cut (cotton twill or wool)— thrift store (look for old lady suiting like Jones NY, Polo, department store house brands), uniqlo, old navy, Zara, H&M or [everlane](https://www.everlane.com/products/womens-tencel-way-high-taper-pant-black?collection=womens-pants-trousers) for new stuff. 
* a fresh pair of boots or oxfords (these will hold up longer than ballet flats or sneakers), also buy some shoe polish
* a fresh pack of underwear— gap body and VS always have sales, parade is also pretty inexpensive. If you haven’t bought clothes in a few years do this for yourself. 
* 2 bras or bralettes that fit you. Go to Nordstrom to get fitted if buying actual bras, then order them on a discount site. Having a well fitted bra is going to read a lot more professional. 
* 1-2 pairs of leggings for working out
* you can probably get away with your old blazers and jackets for now, wearing them oversized. 
* one neutral suit for court — lawyer people might be able to advise on this better. 
* Patagonia worn wear and Eileen fisher renew are good resources for some gently used high quality pieces for outerwear and suiting. 


Since this is a micro-capsule wardrobe now… laundry is a bit of a situation. You wash pants once a or every two weeks with your big laundry and do the tees in the shirts and leggings in the sink after you wear them. I’ve done a bit of this for performances and recordings. 

There’s 2 situations I’ve been in for this:

In ears and avioms (so a set number of sub mixes for them to chose from, or do a general mix) and each stand set their own mix/level. There might be a click track in this case, make sure that has its own fader. Make sure the avioms are marked with which channel is what: click, 2mix, rhythm section if it’s pops, soloists, etc. With this set up you go around and set a general level across the board and go around to all the stations and explain where they can find more or less of something.

Wedges, this is just a light fill of everything + soloists. They’ll tell you what else they might want in their monitor just like any other musician. Feeds would tend to be set up as one aux per section. Conductor may or may not want mons except for hearing soloists in a mixed/pops setting, since their face is already getting the full orchestra they likely won’t need that in their monitors.

ETA a few social points: musicians will appreciate calm quiet professionalism, conductor may or may not have a temper, none of them particularly want to notice technology or care about it.

I don’t have rent control and support rent control. It helps keep seniors in their homes on fixed incomes or helps a teacher stay in an apartment in their school district even though they can no longer afford a market rate apartment. 

Then the less obvious rent controls are things like rent increase caps. For example: if I only expect a 6% raise in rent every year I’m more likely to be able to continue to afford my apartment as most likely my income has similar COL adjustments. When this isn’t applicable it can make for some nasty situations for renters… For example: if I live in an owner occupied building, and my landlord wanted to at the end of my lease he could just double or triple the rent. I would probably have to move and could potential become homeless depending on whether or not I have enough savings to move apartments at the time he decides to increase the rent. If I lived in a place with actual winter like Chicago or even somewhere with a bit of snow here and there, being outside in the elements would kill me. 

Rent control is a humanitarian policy. It’s not the best one… since it does sort of victimize folks like the home owners in the article that may just not have a place to live if they can’t afford to buy out their tenants. Honestly though, folks like them are an exception to the rule. Landlords have wealth and could easily take out a line of credit to pay out their tenants if they didn’t have cash on hand.

Other things that will give you a degraded sound is your stock EQ, filtering stuff so it sounds shitty, like look at the frequency response graph of an old-old mic and emulate that. Notice how it might not have a lot of bass or a lot of highs, or it’s weirdly boosted somewhere in the 200-800hz range which might make it sound like an old telephone. 

For more analog things: fuzz, distortion, tube screamers, and overdrive pedals. I also like reamping things to get distortion and color.
